title: LodeStar component diagram
description: LodeStar, a desktop space trading and combat game: the rules are a Rust crate with no engine dependency, and Godot draws them through a GDExtension library that registers the bridge's classes.

components.name: LodeStar
components.responsibility: The whole game: the Rust workspace and the Godot project, built and shipped together.

components.name: Capabilities
components.responsibility: Reusable rules with no outward dependencies: random generators, space maths, ships, the bubble, the pilot, the universe, the market, equipment and flight.

components.name: Features
components.responsibility: Behaviours built from capabilities: saving and loading the pilot, and trading at the market panel.

components.name: Use cases
components.responsibility: A pilot's goals; so far flying in a system, which owns the 12 Hz tick.

components.name: Presentation bridge (lodestar-bridge)
components.responsibility: SimHost: runs the sim under Godot's frame loop, reads input actions and emits tick and mount signals.

components.name: Godot presentation
components.responsibility: The flight scene, the orbit camera, the rigged ship and its post-import script, and the shaders.

components.name: GDExtension library (lodestar-godot)
components.responsibility: The cdylib Godot loads; registers the bridge's classes.

components.name: Godot 4.7 engine
components.responsibility: Renders, reads input and runs the scenes; loads the extension library.

relationships.description: The Godot project's scenes and scripts.
SimHost ticks FlyInSystem with a TickClock and an InputRecord.
Re-exports SimHost so its registration is linked in.
space.tscn holds a SimHost and connects to its ticked and mount_selected signals.
Runs the main scene set in project.godot.
Trading uses the market and the pilot; saving uses the pilot.
